best_for: Developers who already live in a VS Code style editor and want an AI agent that edits across the whole project, and who expect to pay once the free allowance runs out.
description:
Cursor is a code editor built around an AI coding agent, made by Anysphere, whose team calls itself an applied research group working on the future of software development. Cursor says more than half of the Fortune 500 use it, and it holds SOC 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certifications.

Hand a whole task to the agent and review what it did. Agents can use their own computers to build, test and demo a feature end to end, and you can run several in parallel on jobs that take hours or days. Outside the editor, Cursor works in your terminal, takes requests in Slack and reviews pull requests on GitHub.

points.title: Free is a taste, not a workday
points.text: The Free plan includes Agent and Chat with limited usage and no third-party models. Regular daily use quickly points you to a paid tier.

points.title: Paid tiers run on a weekly pool
points.text: Plus is USD 8 a month, Premium USD 30, Super USD 100 and Ultra USD 200. Each tier gets a usage pool that refreshes weekly and is shared with the CLI, Cloud Agents and the Grok apps. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Third-party models cost extra
points.text: Models from other providers are not part of the pool. On Premium and above they are billed at API list price from prepaid credit, and Plus does not offer them at all. Set a spending cap if you use them.

points.title: Bring your VS Code setup
points.text: A one-click import in Cursor Settings brings over extensions, themes, settings and keybindings from VS Code, so switching does not mean starting over.

points.title: Your code goes to model providers
points.text: AI requests send prompts and code context to providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Privacy Mode, which stops your code being used for training, is on by default only for Enterprise teams; individuals and team admins can switch it on.

points.title: Teams pay per seat
points.text: Teams starts at USD 30 per seat a month and adds central billing, usage analytics, team-wide privacy settings and SAML or OIDC single sign-on. Enterprise is priced on request.

points.title: Downgrades are a Windows thing here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 274 versions, for x64 and Arm64, with per-user and all-users installers. macOS lists only the current release (macOS 12 or later), so a Mac downgrade needs another source. Cursor also ships Linux .deb, RPM and AppImage builds that this site does not list.
